Here’s how you can take your existing Neuro Companion Flutter project and turn it into a Windows desktop application, complete with AI-engine integration, state management, PDF/CSV export, voice journaling, and biometric login:

1. Enable Windows Desktop Support

Make sure you’ve got the Flutter Windows tooling installed:

bash
# Enable Windows desktop
flutter config --enable-windows-desktop

# Verify
flutter doctor -v
# └─[✓] Windows Desktop supported by this Flutter installation.

2. Add the Windows Platform Directory

In your project root:

bash
# This will generate the `windows/` folder (if it’s not already there).
flutter create .

You should now see a windows/ directory alongside lib/, android/, ios/, etc.

3. Update Your pubspec.yaml for Windows-Compatible Plugins

Some packages require Windows–specific implementations. Add or verify these dependencies:

yaml
dependencies:
  flutter:
    sdk: flutter

  # State management (if you’re using Provider / Riverpod / Bloc, etc.)
  flutter_riverpod: ^2.0.0  

  # Biometric login on Windows
  local_auth: ^2.1.0
  local_auth_windows: ^0.1.0

  # PDF generation & printing
  pdf: ^4.8.0
  printing: ^5.10.0

  # CSV export
  csv: ^5.0.0
  path_provider: ^2.0.0

  # Voice journaling (speech-to-text)
  speech_to_text: ^5.4.0

  # HTTP / AI-engine calls (probably already in your app)
  http: ^0.13.4

Then run:

bash
flutter pub get

4. Configure Biometric Login (Windows Hello)

In your Dart code—e.g. in your login flow—use local_auth:

dart
import 'package:local_auth/local_auth.dart';

final _auth = LocalAuthentication();

Future<bool> authenticateWithBiometrics() async {
  final canCheck = await _auth.canCheckBiometrics;
  if (!canCheck) return false;

  return await _auth.authenticate(
    localizedReason: 'Unlock Neuro Companion',
    options: const AuthenticationOptions(
      biometricOnly: true,
    ),
  );
}

In your Windows runner (windows/runner/main.cpp), no extra changes are needed—the plugin handles the Windows Hello API under the hood.

5. Implement PDF & CSV Export

PDF

dart
import 'package:pdf/widgets.dart' as pw;
import 'package:printing/printing.dart';

Future<void> exportMoodReportPdf() async {
  final pdf = pw.Document();
  pdf.addPage(
    pw.Page(
      build: (c) => pw.Center(child: pw.Text('My Mood Report')),
    ),
  );
  await Printing.sharePdf(bytes: await pdf.save(), filename: 'mood_report.pdf');
}

CSV

dart
import 'dart:io';
import 'package:csv/csv.dart';
import 'package:path_provider/path_provider.dart';

Future<void> exportMoodCsv(List<List<dynamic>> rows) async {
  final csvData = const ListToCsvConverter().convert(rows);
  final dir = await getApplicationSupportDirectory();
  final file = File('${dir.path}/mood_report.csv');
  await file.writeAsString(csvData);
  // You can then share or open this file via any Windows file picker UI.
}

6. Add Voice Journaling (Speech-to-Text)

dart
import 'package:speech_to_text/speech_to_text.dart' as stt;

class VoiceJournal {
  final stt.SpeechToText _speech = stt.SpeechToText();

  Future<void> startListening(Function(String) onResult) async {
    final available = await _speech.initialize();
    if (!available) return;
    _speech.listen(onResult: (result) {
      onResult(result.recognizedWords);
    });
  }

  void stopListening() => _speech.stop();
}

The speech_to_text plugin supports Windows desktop—just test with a microphone connected.

7. Verify AI-Engine Integration & State Management

  • Your HTTP calls to your backend or OpenAI endpoints work unchanged on Windows.

  • Ensure you’re managing app state (e.g. with Riverpod or Bloc) so UI, AI responses, and journaling flows are consistent across mobile and desktop.

8. Build & Run on Windows

From your project root:

bash
# Run in debug on Windows
flutter run -d windows

# Create a release build (produces an .exe in build\windows\runner\Release)
flutter build windows --release

9. (Optional) Package into an Installer

Use a Windows installer generator like Inno Setup:

  1. Install Inno Setup.

  2. Create a simple script (installer.iss):

    iss
    [Setup]
AppName=Neuro Companion
AppVersion=1.0
DefaultDirName={pf}\Neuro Companion
DefaultGroupName=Neuro Companion

[Files]
Source: "build\windows\runner\Release\*"; DestDir: "{app}"; Flags: recursesubdirs

[Icons]
Name: "{group}\Neuro Companion"; Filename: "{app}\Neuro Companion.exe"

  3. Compile with Inno Setup and distribute the resulting .exe installer.

  2. Polish the Windows-specific UI (menus, keyboard shortcuts, window size).

  3. Automate your CI/CD to build Windows artifacts on each commit (e.g., GitHub Actions runners on Windows).

Windows Integration

Neuro Companion Windows Desktop Integration

This document provides the complete, ready-to-copy code, configuration, and integration steps to transform your existing Flutter-based Neuro Companion app into a fully functional Windows desktop application—bundling all phases, upgrades, and enhancements we’ve built over its entire development history.

1. Enable Windows Desktop Support

flutter doctor -v # verify Windows support

2. Generate the Windows Platform Folder

In your project root:

flutter create . # adds `windows/` if missing

You should now have windows/, alongside android/, ios/, lib/, etc.

3. pubspec.yaml: Complete Dependency List

Include everything your app uses, desktop-optimized:

dependencies:
flutter:
sdk: flutter

# State management & DI
flutter_riverpod: ^2.0.0

# Core services & HTTP
http: ^0.13.4
dio: ^5.0.0

# Biometric auth
local_auth: ^2.1.0
local_auth_windows: ^0.1.0

# Secure storage & encryption
flutter_secure_storage: ^8.0.0

# AI & backend
openai_api: ^1.0.0 # or your custom AI client

# Real-time sync (if using Firebase)
firebase_core: ^2.0.0
firebase_auth: ^4.0.0
cloud_firestore: ^4.0.0
firebase_storage: ^11.0.0

# Ritual & analytics
fl_chart: ^0.60.0
charts_flutter: ^0.12.0

# PDF generation & printing
pdf: ^4.8.0
printing: ^5.10.0

# CSV export & file IO

Then:

flutter pub get

4. Azure Storage Service & Error Handling

File: lib/services/azure_storage_service.dart

import 'package:azblob/azblob.dart';
import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';

class AzureStorageService {
final BlobServiceClient _client;

AzureStorageService(String connectionString)
: _client = BlobServiceClient.fromConnectionString(connectionString);

Future<List<String>> listContainers() async {
try {
final pager = _client.listBlobContainers();
final names = <String>[];
await for (final c in pager) names.add(c.name);
return names;
} catch (e, st) {
debugPrint('Azure listing error: $e');
throw Exception('Storage access failed');
}
}

// ... other methods with try/catch and logging
}

5. State Management & Dependency Injection

Use Riverpod for global services and AI engine:

final authServiceProvider = Provider<AuthService>((_) => AuthService());
final azureServiceProvider = Provider<AzureStorageService>((_) =>
AzureStorageService(Platform.environment['AZURE_CONN']!));
final aiClientProvider = Provider<OpenAIClient>((_) => OpenAIClient(apiKey: '...'));

Wrap your MaterialApp in ProviderScope:

WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();

}

6. Biometric Login & Data Encryption

AuthService (Windows Hello via local_auth): see previous snippet.

SecureStorageService:

import 'package:flutter_secure_storage/flutter_secure_storage.dart';

class SecureStorageService {
final _storage = const FlutterSecureStorage();
Future<void> write(String key, String value) => _storage.write(key: key, value: value);
Future<String?> read(String key) => _storage.read(key: key);
}

7. Privacy & Auth Flow

Automatically show the Privacy Agreement Screen unless already accepted:

// In your auth flow:
final accepted = await secureStorage.read('privacy_accepted') == 'true';
if (!accepted) Navigator.pushNamed(context, '/privacy');

As per lib/services/voice_journal_service.dart with speech_to_text.

13. PDF & CSV Export Services

Includes both: exportPdfReport() and exportCsv() in ExportService.

Embed a feedback screen (lib/modules/feedback) and log submissions to Firestore.

15. Tests, Coverage & CI/CD

  • Widget tests in test/ and integration tests in integration_test/.

.github/workflows/windows.yml (extends build to run tests and upload coverage badge).

16. Build & Release on Windows

flutter run -d windows # debug
flutter build windows --release # creates .exe in build/windows/runner/Release

See installer.iss script in previous version.

18. Final QA & Checklist

  1. Verify each feature on Windows (auth, AI responses, charts, exports).

  2. Run all tests and confirm ≥ 90% coverage.

Below is a minimal, ready-to-run Flutter Windows app skeleton that you can drop into your repo under a new branch (e.g., windows-model) to verify Windows-specific integration. It includes stubs for each core module.

main.dart

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter_riverpod/flutter_riverpod.dart';
import 'modules/ritual_mode.dart';
import 'modules/goal_tracker.dart';
import 'modules/mood_analytics.dart';
import 'modules/meditation_coach.dart';
import 'modules/therapist_mode.dart';
import 'modules/dashboard.dart';
import 'modules/pay_it_forward.dart';
import 'modules/dream_visualizer.dart';
import 'modules/feedback.dart';
import 'services/auth_service.dart';

void main() {
WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();
runApp(const ProviderScope(child: NeuroWindowsApp()));
}

class NeuroWindowsApp extends ConsumerWidget {
const NeuroWindowsApp({Key? key}) : super(key: key);

@override
Widget build(BuildContext context, WidgetRef ref) {
return MaterialApp(
title: 'Neuro Companion Windows Model',
theme: ThemeData.light(),
home: const DashboardPage(),
routes: {
'/ritual': (_) => const RitualModePage(),
'/goals': (_) => const GoalTrackerPage(),
'/mood': (_) => const MoodAnalyticsPage(),
'/meditation': (_) => const MeditationCoachPage(),
'/therapist': (_) => const TherapistModePage(),
'/payitforward': (_) => const PayItForwardPage(),
'/dream': (_) => const DreamVisualizerPage(),
'/feedback': (_) => const FeedbackPage(),

Stub Modules (e.g., lib/modules/ritual_mode.dart)

Repeat similar stubs for each module (goal_tracker.dart, mood_analytics.dart, etc.), changing titles and placeholder text.

Running the Model

  1. Switch to your windows-model branch.

  2. Ensure windows/ directory exists: flutter create .

  3. Run: flutter pub get && flutter run -d windows

  4. Click through Dashboard links to verify stubs.

This skeleton lets you confirm a working Windows build with all navigation and module placeholders set up. From here, gradually replace each stub with your real implementation.
